facts.raw_span: bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
CD4 count was 24 cells/mm3
HIV RNA level was 175,000 copies/mL
pruritic back rash of crusting erythematous plaques
uncorrected visual acuity was hand motions in both eyes
intraocular pressures were 14 and 9 mm Hg in the right and left eye, respectively
corneal stromal haze, 3+ anterior chamber cell
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details
Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay: positive
Rapid plasma reagin testing: 1:64 titer
interface dermatitis with spirochetes evident upon hematoxylin-eosin staining
Aqueous fluid from both eyes negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR

concepts.why: The patient has a positive Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and a high Rapid plasma reagin testing titer, indicating syphilis infection, which is consistent with the diagnosis of Syphilitic Uveitis.
The patient has a low CD4 count and a high HIV RNA level, indicating advanced HIV disease, which increases the risk of HIV-related Uveitis.

The patient has a positive Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and a high Rapid plasma reagin testing titer, indicating syphilis infection, which is consistent with the diagnosis of Syphilitic Chorioretinitis.
The patient has a low CD4 count and a high HIV RNA level, indicating advanced HIV disease, and is at risk of developing Immune Recovery Uveitis.
It explains the vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details found in the patient's eyes.
It explains the decreased vision, abnormal intraocular pressures, and negative PCR results for herpetic viral DNA in the aqueous fluid.
